evals.prompt: I recorded a 95-second screen demo of my app LedgerLens (an AI expense-audit tool for finance teams). The recording harness emitted these milestones: 0.0s OPEN_DASHBOARD (queue shows 800 receipts pending review); 6.5s RUN_AUDIT (bulk audit runs, queue collapses to 27 flagged); 21.0s OPEN_RECEIPT (one flagged receipt opens: duplicate-vendor pattern); 38.0s EVIDENCE_TRAIL (side-by-side of two duplicate invoices, $4,980 each, different PO numbers); 61.0s APPROVE_FLAG (reviewer confirms the flag; case sealed with an audit record); 78.0s NEXT_CASE_RECALL (the next similar receipt opens and cites the case just confirmed); 95.0s END. Write the voiceover narration to record over this video.
evals.expected_output: Numbered narration segments keyed to the milestone windows, each fitting its window at voiceover pace, spelled-out numbers, recorded register, closing on the product name.
assertions: Segmented with timestamp windows that match the given milestones (approx 0:00->0:06, 0:06->0:21, 0:21->0:38, 0:38->1:01, 1:01->1:18, 1:18->1:35)
Every segment fits its window at voiceover pace: segment word count <= window_seconds x 2.8
Numbers are spelled out for the voice artist (eight hundred, twenty-seven), not digits
Recorded register: present tense describing the screen, no stage cues like (pause) and no audience address
The close lands the product name

evals.prompt: I need a crisp demo video of my web app (localhost:3000, finance dashboard with a canvas chart) for a hackathon submission. I tried my browser automation library's built-in video recording with deviceScaleFactor: 2 but the result looks soft and blocky fullscreen. Ubuntu server. Explain what went wrong and give me a working recording script.
evals.expected_output: Correct diagnosis (CSS-viewport capture + bitrate starvation), a framebuffer-capture script (Xvfb + ffmpeg x11grab, DSF 2, CRF encode, -draw_mouse 0), and frame-verification guidance.
assertions: Diagnoses why screencast recording + a device scale factor is soft: CSS-viewport-sized capture and/or encoder bitrate starvation (not just 'raise the resolution')
Proposes real-framebuffer capture (Xvfb + ffmpeg x11grab or equivalent), not upscaling the existing file
The script hides or deliberately handles the cursor (-draw_mouse 0)
The script uses CRF-controlled encoding rather than default bitrate
Recommends visually verifying extracted frames before shipping

evals.prompt: I'm pitching LedgerLens, my AI expense-audit app, at a fintech hackathon this Friday. I have a 4-minute slot (everything included), a working app, but no demo video and no deck yet. My teammate Sam will be on stage with me. Help me prepare the whole pitch.
evals.expected_output: Interview questions / explicit assumptions first, an explicit 4:00 budget line, a composition plan routing to deck/demo/script work, trim points and a fallback, a speaker plan - and NOT a full deck dump in the first response.
assertions: Leads with interview questions or explicitly stated assumptions BEFORE any artifact content
Contains an explicit time-budget line decomposing the 4:00 slot (spoken + demo + buffer)
Does NOT produce a full deck (HTML or complete slide-by-slide copy) in this first response
Names trim points and/or a demo fallback plan
Includes a speaker plan for the two presenters (who says what, team intro placement)

evals.prompt: Record me a demo video of my app (localhost:5173) for a hackathon submission due tonight. It's an AI research agent - the killer feature is that it remembers what it learned from previous sessions and cites it. Just make the video, I trust you.
evals.expected_output: A storyboard table (screen | action | proof | narration | duration) covering the whole user journey, presented for approval, with the recording explicitly NOT started until the user responds.
assertions: Produces a storyboard BEFORE recording anything, with all five columns: screen, action, proof, narration draft, duration
Explicitly stops and asks for approval of the storyboard; does not proceed to capture in the same turn despite 'I trust you'
Storyboard covers the whole journey (entry / setup / core loop / payoff), not only the memory-recall feature
Does NOT propose title cards, intro slides, logo bookends, or caption overlays as part of the demo film

Identifies that 'remembers what it learned' needs visible on-screen evidence (memory panel, citation, or session history) and plans a beat that shows it - not a status label in which the app merely asserts it remembered
If it previews later steps at all, the smoke take precedes the full capture (it must NOT actually smoke-test or record before approval)

evals.prompt: My demo recording is done (recordings/demo.mp4) and the beats were: open at 0s, run at 8s, results at 22s, close at 35s - those are the holds I set in the script. Write the voiceover to those timestamps so I can record it tonight.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to narrate against planned holds; derives real timestamps from the MP4 and verifies each milestone frame before any narration is written.
assertions: Does NOT write narration against the supplied planned-hold timestamps
Explains that planned holds drift from the delivered file (ffmpeg spin-up, dropped frames, backend latency variance)
Derives real timestamps from the MP4 itself (ffprobe duration / reconciliation / frame extraction), not from the beat list
Extracts and visually checks the frame at each milestone to confirm the expected screen is there before narrating
Routes correctly: treats this as narration work gated on demo-video's verified timestamps, rather than re-recording the video
